documents.title: Follow-up: iron deficiency anemia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Iron f/u. Taking ferrous sulfate nightly, missed a few doses over break. Energy clearly better, stairs at school no longer winding her, dizziness gone. Some constipation, manageable. Colitis quiet - formed stools, no blood in weeks. Still vegan.

Vitals as charted. Color better. Heart regular, murmur not appreciated today. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender.

Labs this AM: Hgb and ferritin both up from November, still below normal. MCV rising.

A/P: IDA responding to oral iron. Continue daily. Recheck CBC/iron at the physical in May. B12 then too. UC per GI, on mesalamine.
Physical in May.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL - 28F

Interval: doing well overall. Energy much improved on iron. For the last few weeks her stools have been looser again, 2-3 a day, no blood, no night waking. She sent GI a message and they said to keep the mesalamine going and call if it worsens; next GI visit is in the fall.
Diet: vegan, no B12 or other supplement still. Exercise: walks most evenings.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap 2019 normal - due today.
Mood fine, PHQ-9 2. Former smoker, no relapse. Alcohol rare.

Current meds: mesalamine DR 800 mg TID (GI); ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA.
FH: father Crohn disease, mother RA, paternal aunt hypothyroidism.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. HEENT normal, no oral ulcers. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal appearing, Pap collected. Skin clear, shins normal. Joints normal. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance: Pap today. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening today. Lipids. Tdap 2016, current. COVID vaccinated with booster. Flu in the fall.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - CBC, iron studies today. Continue iron.
3. Ulcerative colitis - mild loosening of stools, GI aware; she will call them if bleeding or more frequent stools.
4. Vegan diet - B12 today; she would rather take a pill than injections if low.

Will message results.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (1000 mcg) by mouth daily

documents.title: Lab results: B12 low
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with results. B12 182, low (was low-normal in November) - dietary, from a strict vegan diet with no supplement. No numbness, tingling, balance trouble or memory change per her. Hgb now in the normal range and ferritin up again, iron is working. Lipids, CMP fine. HIV and hep C negative.
Plan: cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg by mouth daily (sent to pharmacy; vegan formulations are easy to find). Recheck B12 in 3-6 months, at the latest with next physical. Continue iron. Pap pending.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap smear is normal. Routine schedule from here; we will talk about timing at your next physical. Enjoy the end of the school year.

documents.title: Stomach getting worse
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, since the start of the school year my stomach has gotten worse. Up to 5 or 6 loose BMs a day, sometimes a little blood, cramping on the right side, and I've lost about 5 lbs. I'm still taking the mesalamine every day. My GI appointment isn't until the end of November. Should I be doing something sooner?

documents.title: RE: Stomach getting worse
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. I have sent a note to your GI office asking them to move you up or call you about a plan in the meantime; please also call them directly today since they manage the mesalamine. If you have a fever, can't keep fluids down, have a lot of blood, or the pain becomes severe, go to the ED. Update: I spoke with GI - the date you hold is their soonest colonoscopy slot, you are on their cancellation list, and their nurse will call you about a plan until then.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal vaccines. Afebrile, feels OK aside from her bowels (GI aware, colonoscopy late November). Flu quadrivalent IM L deltoid; Pfizer bivalent COVID booster IM R deltoid. VIS reviewed. Waited 15 min, no reaction.

conditions.label: Crohn disease
conditions.note: Colonic skip lesions, granulomas, perianal fistula; initially labeled ulcerative colitis

medications.sig: Take 8 tablets (40 mg) by mouth daily, then decrease by 1 tablet each week until off

reports.text: Indication: worsening diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss in a patient carrying a diagnosis of ulcerative colitis. Moderate sedation. Prep adequate. Perianal inspection: external opening of a draining fistula. Scope advanced to the cecum and terminal ileum. Discontinuous areas of inflamed mucosa with erythema and ulceration in the colon, separated by segments of normal-appearing mucosa. Biopsies from inflamed and normal-appearing segments.
reports.conclusion: Patchy colitis with intervening normal mucosa and a perianal fistula, favoring Crohn disease. Biopsies sent.

reports.text: A-D. Colon, multiple sites, biopsies: chronic active colitis, patchy, with noncaseating granulomas in two of four sites; intervening biopsies with minimal change. No dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Chronic active colitis with noncaseating granulomas, consistent with Crohn disease.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up and colonoscopy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP VISIT
Date of service: 11/29/2022

Ms. Shapiro returns, last seen here June 2021 for what was labeled left-sided ulcerative colitis, with iron deficiency anemia since diagnosed by her PCP in November 2021.

She reports six months of intermittent abdominal pain and diarrhea with steady weight loss, much worse over the last two months: up to six loose stools daily, sometimes with blood. Taking mesalamine 800 mg TID reliably, plus iron and B12.

FH: father with Crohn disease. SH: former smoker, quit 2020.

Exam: afebrile. Weight down from last visit. Abdomen: tender in the right lower quadrant, no rebound or guarding. Perianal exam: a draining fistula.
Labs: Hgb 11.2, WBC 9.5, CRP 24 mg/L, ESR 40.
Colonoscopy today: skip areas of inflamed colon between normal segments; perianal fistula. Pathology 12/2: noncaseating granulomas.

Impression: Crohn disease of the colon with perianal fistula. The earlier picture read as ulcerative colitis; with skip lesions, granulomas and fistulizing disease, we are revising the diagnosis to Crohn disease.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 40 mg daily, decrease 5 mg each week to off over 8 weeks.
2. Start infliximab 5 mg/kg IV (weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks) - preferred with the fistula. Before the first dose we need QuantiFERON, hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody; we have asked her PCP's office to draw these. Recommend inactivated vaccines (pneumococcal, recombinant zoster) before starting; no live vaccines on therapy.
3. Continue mesalamine 800 mg TID for now.
4. Continue oral iron and B12.
5. Return 2-3 months after induction.

Allergies: NKDA.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI request: pre-biologic labs
documents.author: RN
documents.body: GI nurse called: pt starting infliximab early January, asks us to draw QuantiFERON, HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs, results faxed to them. Also asking for pneumococcal and Shingrix before first infusion if possible. Orders entered per PCP. Called pt - coming tomorrow AM for labs, will book nurse visit for vaccines.

documents.title: Lab draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Venipuncture R antecubital, one attempt. QuantiFERON tubes shaken and kept at room temp per protocol, sent with courier. Hep B panel sent. Pt tolerated well. Results to be faxed to GI on return.

documents.title: Nervous about infliximab
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi Doctor, honestly I'm a little freaked out. Crohn's like my dad, and now an IV drug every two months. I read about infections and lymphoma. Did my tests come back OK? Is it safe for me to be around 25 seven-year-olds all winter? The prednisone is helping already, which is good.

documents.title: RE: Nervous about infliximab
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Very understandable to feel this way. Your TB test and hepatitis B tests are fine - no TB exposure, no hepatitis B, and you are immune from your childhood shots; GI has the results. Infliximab is a standard and effective treatment for Crohn disease with a fistula, and the serious risks are uncommon; GI will go over them in detail. Classroom life is fine. Hand-washing, your yearly flu shot (done) and COVID boosters (done) help, and you should call us with any fever. Next step here: the pneumonia vaccine and the first shingles shot at a nurse visit next week, both non-live and safe before infliximab. We are here for questions anytime.

documents.title: PCV20 and Shingrix #1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pre-infliximab vaccines per PCP and GI. On prednisone taper (now 35 mg). Afebrile. PCV20 IM L deltoid. Shingrix dose 1 IM R deltoid. Explained sore arm/fatigue for 1-2 days possible with Shingrix. Dose 2 due in 1-2 months; she will get it at her February visit. No reaction during 15-min observation.
